A constant-error Rayleigh quotient gives a distribution-independent upper bound on the minimum spectral improvement. Uniform sampling produces a symmetric circulant averaged update with nonnegative entries, so its constant row-sum eigenvalue is the top eigenvalue; this attains the bound. Direct Green-function recurrence and finite cosh sum yield the exact rate, and a justified joint q-alpha limit yields the hyperbolic crossover. Reconstructed algebra is supported by 23429 independent exact-fraction and floating-limit checks, not dependent on finite enumeration.
